subject: Add polygon to leaflet map by accessing API

messages.author: 33fe3608622d7c76
messages.subject: Add polygon to leaflet map by accessing API
parts:
Hello!

I am building a Shiny web app that starts with the base code provided in this example: http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/superzip-example.html 

I would like to be able to add a polygon to the base map by using the StreamStats API (which provides a geojson file): http://streamstatsags.cr.usgs.gov/streamstatsservices/watershed.geojson?rcode=NY&xlocation=-73.8377&ylocation=43.9572&crs=4326&includeparameters=false&includeflowtypes=false&includefeatures=true&simplify=true

Here is a chunk of the code I've started to develop for this task:
server.r

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  #StreamStats Data
  SS_geojson <- reactive({
    SS_link <- "http://streamstatsags.cr.usgs.gov/streamstatsservices/watershed.geojson?rcode=NY&xlocation=-73.8377&ylocation=43.9572&crs=4326&includeparameters=false&includeflowtypes=false&includefeatures=true&simplify=true"
    geojson <- readLines(SS_link,warn='F') %>% paste(collapse='\n') %>% fromJSON(simplifyVector=FALSE)
  })
  
  ## Interactive Map ###########################################
 
  # Create the map
  output$map <- renderLeaflet({
    leaflet() %>%
      addTiles(
        urlTemplate = "//{s}.tiles.mapbox.com/v3/jcheng.map-5ebohr46/{z}/{x}/{y}.png",
        attribution = 'Maps by <a href="http://www.mapbox.com/">Mapbox</a>'
      ) %>% 
      setView(lng = -74.2890, lat = 43.3582, zoom = 7)%>%
      addGeoJSON(SS_geojson(),fillColor="red")    
  })
...

This code runs, but the polygon never shows up. I am not sure if I need to format the geojson file once I access it or what the problem is exactly, but any help or direction is greatly appreciated. 

Thanks in advance!

Sarah

messages.author: dc3c7e88d9ea3297
messages.subject: Re: Add polygon to leaflet map by accessing API
parts:
Looks like you've got FeatureCollections inside FeatureCollections which is not valid GeoJSON AFAIK. You can use http://geojsonlint.com/ or https://github.com/ropensci/geojsonio to look into it.

For the first FeatureCollection, you'll want to parse out:

{"type": "FeatureCollection",
        "crs": {
          "type": "ESPG",
          "properties": {
            "code": 4326
          }
        },
        "features": [
          {
            "properties": {
              "objectid": 1,
              "hydroid": 1,
              "drainid": 2,
              "hucid": "02020001",
              "name": "ags101"
            },
            "type": "Feature",
            "bbox": [
              -73.837555857376984,
              43.95738070271539
            ],
            "geometry": {
              "type": "Point",
              "coordinates": [
                -73.837555857376984,
                43.95738070271539
              ]
            }
          }
        ]
      }

And handle the second FeatureCollection similarly (right after "feature": ). You could then pull both of these into a valid GeoJSON just by manipulating the string, or use sp (SpatialPolygonsDataFrame) + geojsonio.

Chris

parts:
I'm guessing you just need the "globalwatershed". This would get more complicated if it returned more than one watershed, but:

dat <- readLines("countries.json") %>% 
       jsonlite::fromJSON(simplifyDataFrame = FALSE) %>% 
       .[["featurecollection"]]
geojsonList <- Filter(function(x) x["name"]=="globalwatershed",dat)[[1]][["feature"]]
geojsonJSON <- jsonlite::toJSON(geojsonList,auto_unbox = TRUE,digits=5)
leaflet() %>% 
  addTiles() %>% 
  setView(-73.83, 44.10, zoom = 10) %>% 
  addGeoJSON(geojsonJSON) # or addGeoJSON(geojsonList)

FWIW, you may want to keep an eye on performance going to JSON (from toJSON within addGeoJSON or outside of it as in geojsonJSON here).

Chris

Great, thank you so much for your help!



On Friday, February 5, 2016 at 2:07:36 PM UTC-5, hol...@geocf.com wrote:
Looks like you've got FeatureCollections inside FeatureCollections which is not valid GeoJSON AFAIK. You can use http://geojsonlint.com/ or https://github.com/ropensci/geojsonio to look into it.

For the first FeatureCollection, you'll want to parse out:

{"type": "FeatureCollection",
        "crs": {
          "type": "ESPG",
          "properties": {
            "code": 4326
          }
        },
        "features": [
          {
            "properties": {
              "objectid": 1,
              "hydroid": 1,
              "drainid": 2,
              "hucid": "02020001",
              "name": "ags101"
            },
            "type": "Feature",
            "bbox": [
              -73.837555857376984,
              43.95738070271539
            ],
            "geometry": {
              "type": "Point",
              "coordinates": [
                -73.837555857376984,
                43.95738070271539
              ]
            }
          }
        ]
      }

And handle the second FeatureCollection similarly (right after "feature": ). You could then pull both of these into a valid GeoJSON just by manipulating the string, or use sp (SpatialPolygonsDataFrame) + geojsonio.

Chris
